text: Either party may terminate this contract by giving the other party four weeks' written notice.
The notice period for termination shall be two months for the Employee and two months for the Company.
Employment may be ended by either party by serving 60 days notice in writing.
Should the Employee wish to resign, the Company must be told at least one month before the final working day.
The Company may end this contract on giving the Employee six weeks' prior warning of the end date.
Resignation takes effect only after the Employee has worked out the full two months stated in the offer letter.
The Employee shall be entitled to 14 days of annual leave per calendar year.
Annual leave entitlement increases to 16 days after five years of service.
Paid leave of 12 days per year shall be granted after the first year of service.
After completing a year with the Company, the Employee may take twelve working days away from work each year without loss of pay.
Holiday entitlement under this contract is 18 working days, to be scheduled with the manager's approval.
Time away for rest and recreation, fully paid, accrues at one day per month of service.
The Employee is entitled to 14 days of paid sick leave per year on production of a medical certificate.
Hospitalisation leave of up to 60 days shall be provided where the Employee is warded.
Absence due to illness must be supported by a medical certificate from a registered practitioner.
If the Employee is unwell and cannot work, the Company will keep paying salary for up to fourteen days a year.
Where a doctor orders bed rest, the Employee remains on full pay for the days stated by the doctor, subject to the annual cap.
Time away for treatment in hospital is covered for up to sixty days in addition to ordinary absence for ill health.
A female Employee is entitled to 98 days of maternity leave for each confinement.
Paternity leave of seven days shall be granted to married male employees.
Maternity benefit shall be paid in accordance with the Employment Act 1955.
A mother-to-be shall be given 98 consecutive days away from work around the birth of her child, on full pay.
New fathers may claim seven days of paid absence after their wife gives birth.
The Company recognises the needs of new parents and will follow the statutory minimums for time away after a baby arrives.
Normal working hours are 8 hours per day, Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm.
The Employee shall not be required to work more than 45 hours per week.
The Employee may be required to work in shifts as determined by the Company.
The Employee is expected at the office from nine in the morning until six in the evening on weekdays.
A working week under this contract shall not exceed forty-five hours, spread over five or six days.
Daily attendance is from 8.30am to 5.30pm with a one hour lunch break.
Overtime shall be paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate of pay for work on normal days.
Overtime pay for work on rest days is 2 times the ordinary rate.
Any extra hours worked must be approved in advance and will be compensated.
Work done after the normal finishing time will be paid at one and a half times the hourly rate.
Employees earning RM 4,000 or less are paid more for any time worked past the standard day, at premium rates set by law.
The Company will not require more than 104 additional hours a month, and these must be paid at the statutory multiplier.
The Employee is entitled to one rest day in every week.
Sunday shall be the weekly rest for all employees.
The Employee shall have two days off each week, Saturday and Sunday.
Each week the Employee must be given one full day free from all work duties.
No employee shall be made to work seven days in a row without a free day.
Saturdays and Sundays are not working days unless the Company states otherwise in writing.
The Employee is entitled to all gazetted holidays declared by the Federal Government.
The Employee shall be entitled to at least eleven paid public holidays per year including National Day.
Cuti umum shall be observed in accordance with the Holidays Act 1951.
The office is closed on Hari Raya, Deepavali, Chinese New Year and other days declared by the government as days of national observance.
If a festival day falls on a Sunday, the next working day shall be given in its place.
Work on a day the government has set aside for celebration shall be paid at three times the daily rate.
The Employee shall receive a monthly salary of RM 4,000 payable on the last working day of each month.
Salary payment shall be made by bank transfer not later than the seventh day after the end of the wage period.
The Company shall pay all wages through payroll on the 25th of every month.
The Employee will be paid RM 3,200 at the end of each calendar month into the bank account given to HR.
Pay shall be credited no later than the seventh day after the month ends.
Compensation for the work done will be transferred on the final working day of every month.
The Company may make deductions from the Employee's salary for any loss or damage caused by the Employee.
Any advance given to the Employee shall be recovered through salary deduction in full.
The Company reserves the right to withhold wages pending the return of company property.
Where the Employee owes the Company money for any reason, the Company may take it out of the Employee's pay without further notice.
Training costs will be taken back from the Employee's pay, up to the full amount, if the Employee leaves within two years.
The Company may keep back part of the final month's pay to cover any shortfall.
The Employee shall serve a probationary period of three months from the commencement date.
Upon successful completion of probation the Employee shall be confirmed in writing.
The Company may extend the probation by up to three months.
The first six months of employment are a trial period, during which the Company will assess suitability for the role.
After three months the Company will decide whether to offer the Employee a permanent position.
During the initial trial period the Employee's performance will be reviewed monthly by the manager.
The Employee agrees to a non-compete obligation for 24 months after leaving the Company.
The Employee shall not, for two years after termination, engage in any competing business in Malaysia.
This restrictive covenant shall apply to all employees at manager level and above.
After leaving, the Employee must not work for any firm in the same industry for a period of 18 months.
The Employee shall not approach the Company's clients or persuade its staff to resign for 12 months after the last working day.
For two years following the end of employment, the Employee may not set up or join any similar venture anywhere in South-East Asia.
The Company has adopted a sexual harassment policy and shall conduct an inquiry on every complaint.
The Employee shall comply with the Company's code of conduct at all times.
Workplace harassment of any kind is prohibited and will result in disciplinary action.
Unwelcome advances or comments of a sexual nature are not tolerated, and complaints will be investigated by a panel.
The Company will treat any report of improper behaviour of a sexual nature privately and act on it promptly.
Employees who feel they have been made uncomfortable by a colleague's behaviour can lodge a complaint with HR.
This contract shall be governed by the laws of Malaysia.
The courts of Malaysia shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising from this contract.
Any dispute shall be settled by arbitration in Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysian courts alone may decide any disagreement that arises under this agreement.
Any claim relating to this contract will be heard in Kuala Lumpur under Malaysian legislation.
Disagreements shall first be referred to mediation and, if unresolved, to the Industrial Court.
The Employee shall keep all confidential information of the Company secret during and after employment.
The Employee agrees to sign a non-disclosure agreement upon commencement.
The Employee shall not disclose any trade secret or proprietary information to third parties.
Nothing learned about the Company's customers, pricing or plans may be shared with outsiders, even after leaving.
The Employee must not pass on any internal documents or client lists to anyone outside the Company.
All know-how acquired in the course of work shall remain private, and this duty survives termination.
The Company shall contribute to the Employees Provident Fund at the rate of 13% of monthly wages.
Both parties shall make mandatory contributions to KWSP as required by law.
EPF contributions will be deducted from salary and remitted by the 15th of each month.
The Company will pay into the Employee's retirement savings account at the rate required by statute.
A portion of the Employee's pay is set aside each month for old age savings, matched by the employer as the law requires.
Statutory pension contributions for the Employee will be paid by the employer every month.
The Company shall register the Employee under SOCSO and pay the required contributions.
The Employee is covered under the Employment Insurance System (EIS) in accordance with law.
PERKESO contributions shall be shared between employer and employee as prescribed.
The Company shall enrol the Employee in the national scheme that provides benefits if the Employee is injured or disabled.
Contributions to the government social protection scheme will be paid by both sides every month.
Upon loss of job, the Employee may claim benefits under the national job-loss protection scheme.
The monthly salary shall not be less than the minimum wage of RM 1,700 prescribed by law.
The Company confirms that the basic wage paid complies with the Minimum Wages Order 2022.
In no case shall the Employee be paid below the minimum salary fixed by the government.
The Employee's pay will always meet or exceed the lowest rate that the law allows an employer to pay.
The Company undertakes that earnings will never fall under the statutory floor, currently RM 1,700 a month.
If the legal wage floor is raised, the Employee's pay will be increased to match.
The Company shall pay the HRDF levy in respect of the Employee as required by law.
The Company is registered with HRD Corp and the Employee may attend approved training.
The Employee is eligible for training funded by the training levy.
The Company contributes to the national skills development fund and will support the Employee's approved courses.
Employees may apply for sponsored courses, which the Company recovers from a government scheme to which it pays a levy.
A monthly contribution of 1% of wages is paid by the employer for workforce skills upgrading.
The Company shall be liable for any workplace injury suffered by the Employee in the course of employment.
Compensation for industrial accident shall be paid in accordance with the Workmen's Compensation Act.
The Company maintains personal accident insurance for all employees.
If the Employee is hurt while carrying out duties, the Company will pay for treatment and lost income.
Medical expenses arising from an accident occurring during working hours will be borne by the Company or its insurer.
The Employee is protected by the Company's insurance if harmed on the job.
This Employment Contract is entered into between ABC Technology Sdn. Bhd. (the Company) and the Employee named in the Schedule.
The Employee is employed as a Software Developer commencing 1 January 2026.
The Employee shall report to the Head of Engineering or any person designated by the Company.
The Employee shall perform the duties set out in the job description and any other reasonable duties assigned by the Company.
The Employee shall devote full time and attention to the business of the Company.
This contract constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior discussions.
No amendment to this contract shall be valid unless made in writing and signed by both parties.
If any provision of this contract is held to be invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in force.
The Employee shall return all company equipment, including laptops and access cards, on the last day of employment.
Signed by the parties on the date first written above.
The Employee declares that all information given during recruitment is true and accurate.
Any notice required under this contract shall be sent to the address stated in the Schedule.
The Employee shall inform the Company in writing of any change in residential address or contact number.
The Employee may be required to travel within Malaysia for business purposes, with expenses reimbursed by the Company.
The Company shall provide a laptop and a mobile phone for work purposes.
The Employee shall comply with all reasonable instructions and safety rules while on the Company's premises.
The Employee shall not accept gifts from suppliers above RM 200 without approval.
The Employee is entitled to a staff discount of 10% on the Company's products.
The Company may require the Employee to attend training sessions during working hours.
The Employee's job title and department may be changed by the Company from time to time.
Disputes between colleagues at the workplace shall first be raised with the immediate supervisor.
The tenancy period shall be twelve months commencing on 1 March 2026 and ending on 28 February 2027.
The term of tenancy is two years, with the commencement date being 1 June 2026.
The tenancy shall commence on the start date stated in the Schedule and continue until the expiry date.
The Tenant may occupy the premises for one year starting from the day the keys are handed over.
This agreement runs for 24 months, beginning 15 July 2026.
The Tenant's right to stay in the property lasts from 1 January 2027 until 31 December 2027.
The monthly rent shall be RM 2,200 payable by the Tenant to the Landlord.
The rental amount is RM 1,800 per month, inclusive of maintenance fees.
Rent of RM 3,000 per month shall be paid without any set-off.
The Tenant agrees to pay the Landlord RM 2,500 every month for the use of the property.
For the use of the unit, the Tenant shall hand over RM 1,500 monthly.
The sum payable each month for occupation is RM 2,000, fixed for the first year.
The Tenant shall pay a security deposit equivalent to two months' rent upon signing this agreement.
The deposit is refundable within 14 days after the Tenant vacates, less any deductions for damage.
A damage deposit of RM 4,400 shall be held by the Landlord during the tenancy.
On signing, the Tenant shall give the Landlord RM 5,000 to be held as security and returned when the tenancy ends.
The Landlord holds two months' rent as a safeguard against unpaid rent or damage and will give it back at the end if nothing is owed.
A one-off sum equal to three months of rent is kept by the Landlord to cover any breach by the Tenant.
The Tenant shall pay a utility deposit of RM 500, refundable upon settlement of all outstanding bills.
A water deposit and an electricity deposit shall be paid directly to the respective providers.
The Tenant shall settle every utility bill before the end of the tenancy.
An additional sum of RM 300 is payable to cover unpaid water, power and internet charges at the end of the tenancy.
The Tenant shall place a further sum aside for outstanding charges of gas, water and electricity.
A separate refundable amount is collected to guarantee payment of the Tenant's electricity and water consumption.
The rent is payable in advance on or before the first of the month.
The due date for rent is the 5th day of each month.
Payment shall be paid on the 7th of every month by bank transfer.
The Tenant must settle each month's rent no later than the fifth day of that month.
Rent for any month falls to be paid before that month begins.
Payments are to reach the Landlord's bank account by the 10th of each month.
This agreement shall be stamped with the Inland Revenue Board within 30 days of signing.
Stamp duty on this agreement shall be borne by the Tenant.
The parties shall ensure this tenancy agreement is duly stamped under the Stamp Act 1949.
The cost of having this agreement registered with the tax authority shall be shared equally between the parties.
The Landlord shall bear the government duty payable on this document.
This agreement is not valid evidence in court until the official government charge on it has been paid.
Either party may terminate this tenancy by giving two months' written notice to the other party.
The notice period for termination is three months.
The Tenant shall give notice to vacate not less than one month before the intended date.
If the Tenant wants to leave before the end of the term, the Landlord must be told at least sixty days beforehand.
Before ending the tenancy, either side must give the other two full months of warning.
The Landlord can require the Tenant to leave only after giving the Tenant ninety days to prepare.
The Landlord shall be responsible for major structural repairs to the premises.
The Tenant shall keep the premises clean and bear the cost of minor maintenance such as changing light bulbs.
The Tenant is not liable for fair wear and tear.
Anything that breaks through ordinary use will be fixed at the Landlord's cost; damage caused by the Tenant's carelessness will be fixed at the Tenant's cost.
The Tenant shall look after the house and promptly tell the Landlord of any leak or fault.
Small fixes under RM 200 are the Tenant's job, and larger works belong to the owner.
The Tenant shall not sublet or assign the premises without the prior written consent of the Landlord.
Subletting of any part of the property is strictly prohibited.
The Tenant is not permitted to sublet or part with possession of the premises.
No other person may be allowed to live in the premises in exchange for rent without the Landlord's agreement.
The Tenant may not hand the property over to somebody else to occupy.
Only the Tenant and the family members named in the Schedule may stay in the unit.
The Landlord may enter the premises for inspection upon giving 24 hours prior notice.
The Landlord has the right to inspect the property once every three months.
The Landlord shall have access to property in an emergency without prior notice.
The owner may visit the unit to check its condition provided the Tenant is told a day beforehand.
In case of fire or flooding, the Landlord may come in at any time without asking.
The Landlord's representatives may show the property to prospective buyers at reasonable times.
The premises shall be used for residential purposes only.
The Tenant shall not use the property for business or commercial activities.
Permitted use: domestic use as a private dwelling.
The unit may be used only as a home for the Tenant and the Tenant's family.
Running a shop, office or any trade from the property is not allowed.
The Tenant must not use the premises for any unlawful or immoral activity.
If the Tenant terminates early, the deposit shall be forfeited in full.
The Tenant shall pay liquidated damages equal to two months' rent for early termination.
A penalty of one month's rent applies if the Tenant leaves before the end of the lock-in period.
A Tenant who moves out before the agreed end date loses the whole of the sum held by the Landlord and must also pay the rent for the remaining months.
Leaving before the lock-in period expires will cost the Tenant three months' rent as a charge.
Should the Tenant end the tenancy sooner than agreed, the Landlord keeps everything paid in advance.
The Tenant may renew the tenancy for a further term of one year by giving two months' notice.
There is an option to renew on terms to be agreed, with rent increased by no more than 10%.
The tenancy may be extended by mutual written agreement.
At the end of the term, the Tenant has first right to stay for another year if the Tenant gives early notice of this wish.
If both sides agree, the Tenant can continue to live in the premises beyond the original period at a revised rent.
The Landlord shall let the Tenant know three months before expiry whether a further term will be offered.
This agreement shall be governed by the laws of Malaysia.
The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Malaysian courts.
Any dispute resolution shall be conducted in Kuala Lumpur.
Any disagreement arising from this tenancy will be decided by the courts of this country.
Malaysian courts alone shall hear claims under this agreement.
Any disputes will be brought before the Magistrate's Court in the district where the property is located.
An inventory list of the furniture and appliances is attached as Schedule 2.
The premises are let fully furnished with the fixtures and fittings listed in the Schedule.
The Tenant acknowledges receipt of the items provided as itemised in the schedule of condition.
A list of everything in the unit, such as the sofa, bed and air-conditioners, forms part of this agreement.
The Tenant has checked the appliances on the first day and agrees with the attached list.
Any item listed in the Schedule that is lost or broken must be replaced by the Tenant at equal value.
Late payment of rent shall attract a late fee of RM 50 per week.
Interest on late payment shall be charged at 8% per annum.
Any overdue rental shall bear a late charge of 1.5% per month.
If rent is not received within seven days of the due date, the Tenant shall pay an additional 5% on the unpaid amount.
Delays in paying rent will cost the Tenant an extra charge of RM 100 for each week of delay.
Rent that remains unpaid after the grace period carries a daily surcharge.
No pets are allowed in the premises without the written consent of the Landlord.
The Tenant may keep one cat, subject to payment of a pet deposit of RM 500.
Dogs are not permitted on the premises.
The Tenant shall not keep any animals in the unit, whether inside or on the balcony.
Household companions such as cats or dogs may be kept only with the owner's agreement.
Keeping birds, fish, or any other living creatures in the premises requires the Landlord's prior approval.
On expiry of the tenancy, the Tenant shall return the property in the same condition as at the start, subject to fair wear and tear.
The Tenant shall give vacant possession of the premises at the end of tenancy.
Upon the Tenant's move out, the Landlord shall inspect the property and the condition of property shall be recorded.
When leaving, the Tenant must leave the house empty, clean, and in the state it was received.
At the close of the agreement, the unit should be handed back with keys and free of the Tenant's belongings.
Before the final day, the Tenant must remove all personal items and have the unit professionally cleaned.
This Tenancy Agreement is made between the Landlord and the Tenant named in the Schedule.
The Landlord is the registered owner of the property described in the Schedule.
This agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties.
No variation of this agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.
If any provision is held invalid, the remaining provisions shall remain in effect.
Signed by the parties on the date first written above.
Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa.
The Tenant shall not cause nuisance or annoyance to neighbouring occupants.
The Tenant shall observe the rules of the management corporation regarding parking and use of common facilities.
The Tenant shall allow only registered vehicles to park in the designated bay.
The Tenant shall not install any satellite dish or alter the exterior of the building.
Any notice under this agreement shall be sent to the address of the party stated in the Schedule.
The Tenant shall inform the Landlord of any change in contact number.
The Landlord shall pay the quit rent and assessment on the property.
The Tenant shall insure personal belongings at the Tenant's own risk.
The Landlord shall not be liable for any loss of the Tenant's belongings.
The Tenant shall comply with all laws and regulations of the relevant local authority.
